decision.explanation: The evidence from pmid-23766237 explicitly reports the prevalence of TERT promoter mutations (specifically C228T) in various types of thyroid cancer. The data shows a significant increase in mutation frequency with tumor aggressiveness: 0% in benign tumors, 11.7% in papillary thyroid cancer (PTC), 11.4% in follicular thyroid cancer (FTC), 37.5% in poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC), and 42.6% in anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC). The text further notes that TERT promoter mutations were significantly more prevalent in aggressive variants (30.8%) compared to classic and follicular variant PTC (10.3%). This pattern supports the claim that TERT promoter mutations are associated with thyroid cancer, particularly in more aggressive forms, aligning with a positive diagnostic or prognostic significance.

citations.quote: We found the C228T mutation in 0 of 85 (0.0%) benign thyroid tumors, 30 of 257 (11.7%) papillary thyroid cancers (PTC), 9 of 79 (11.4%) follicular thyroid cancers (FTC), 3 of 8 (37.5%) poorly differentiated thyroid cancers (PDTC), 23 of 54 (42.6%) anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC), and 8 of 12 (66.7%) thyroid cancer cell lines. . . . As shown in Table 3, TERT promoter mutations were significantly more prevalent in the TCPTC samples than in the CPTC and FVPTC samples, 30.8% (4/13) in the former vs 10.3% (25/243) in the latter two (P=0.046, per two-tailed Fisher's exact test).
